title: Fix various compile errors
body:
I found a few more compile errors so I made some minor fixes.

For the `Window` methods I guess it might make more sense to just keep the alias as-is and change the names in the module itself instead (`setWindowPosCallback` instead of `setPosCallback`), but I'll leave that for you to decide.

As for breaking things:
* I changed `Monitor.getPos` to work just as `Window.getPos`. Return `c_int` as provided by the GLFW API, and return an array instead of a slice.
* `focuswindow` -> `focusWindow`, assuming this was a typo.
author: simeks

comments.body:
Thanks!

For top-level fn names I think we should prefer sticking to how they are named in glfw rather than changing them. As this offers the least surprises for users of that API. For our "scoped aliases" however, we can deviate from underlying api naming somewhat.
Thanks for the quick response! That makes sense, so now I've changed the top-level function names instead.

title: [zglfw] Add bindings for `glfwSetErrorCallback()`
body:
I am switching from mach_glfw to zglfw because of Mach's zig version restrictions which stop ZLS from working. Anyway, I've noticed that apparently, there is no equivalent to `glfwSetErrorCallback`. Am I wrong? If not, I'd like to have such a binding.

Thanks in advance!
author: terraquad

comments.body: Hi! zglfw is checking for errors itself in places and it seems nobody has found themselves reaching for `glfwSetErrorCallback` so far. I'm not sure which flavour of API is better. But we should add a binding for this anyway.

Question, how is one supposed to access the description in the callback? I'm new to zig and don't know C, I was just following the glfw guide for the first time and trying to setup this handler, but I couldn't get the error description to print. Looking at the type (`*?[:0]const u8`) I tried several things, including `desc.*.?` and `orelse`, but I would get weird errors like `General Protection Exception (no address available)`. Looking at other bindings for glfw I saw they typed the callback's description like `[*:0]const u8` which from some googling seems to be how a `const char*` is often typed. I cloned this repo and changed this and I could print the error then.

Are the types right and I'm doing something silly or ?

The type is wrong and should be changed. It should be `?[*:0]const u8`. A nullable pointer to a null-terminated string. Nullable is added to cover the possibly that glfw passes us null for description.
Thanks for pointing this out.
